correctness.rationale: The support-functional characterization exhausts all Birkhoff pairs after octagonal symmetry. At a smooth edge the unique support forces y to the normalized kernel direction, and the two sum norms are affine functions covering the claimed interval. At a vertex the support cone sweeps exactly the two-edge boundary arc between the kernels of the adjacent extreme supports; the four signed arc pieces have explicit norm formulas whose ranges stay inside the same endpoints. Both endpoints are attained by explicit unit Birkhoff-orthogonal pairs. Applying the decreasing affine map z↦1-z/2 gives the stated δ_B and ρ_B values.
risks: The key classification uses the standard supporting-functional characterization of Birkhoff orthogonality; the finite-dimensional polygonal case is also reconstructed directly in the proof.
The result is not a statement about symmetric orthogonality; the orientation x⊥_B y is retained throughout.
sources: AJMAA 20 (2023), No. 1, Art. 2, definition of δ_B and ρ_B and Birkhoff orthogonality

originality.rationale: Searches covered the exact δ_B/ρ_B notation, the equivalent μ'(X) formulation for ρ_B, oriented sup/inf sum norms, the older orthogonal James/Schäffer notation, and regular-octagon aliases. The defining 2023 full text was inspected through the definitions, Radon-plane section, ρ_B relation and conclusion; it treats the affine regular hexagon but contains no regular-octagon computation. The highly relevant 2022 Baronti–Papini full text was inspected at its regular-octagon Example 5.3: it proves J_perp=g_perp=sqrt(2), which controls min/max of the pair of sum and difference lengths but not the separate oriented extrema computed here. No checked public research record states the displayed interval or either derived modulus value.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and research-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent minimum-sum computation may exist under older μ' notation or another Birkhoff sum-length parameter not captured by the checked aliases.
The defining 2023 paper cites a 2022 survey for μ'; no regular-octagon value was located in targeted searches, but the survey was not exhaustively re-read cover to cover.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Du and Li introduced δ_B and ρ_B specifically to quantify how far the midpoint of a Birkhoff-orthogonal unit pair can lie from the sphere and called for further geometric information about these moduli. The regular octagon is a canonical non-Hilbert benchmark already known to have Hilbert-like orthogonal James and Schäffer constants. The exact oriented interval reveals geometry that those symmetric constants miss: its two endpoints are unequal around sqrt(2), and the derived moduli satisfy the simple structural identity ρ_B=3δ_B. The support-cone decomposition is reusable for other polygonal Birkhoff-modulus calculations.
risks: This is an exact canonical benchmark and structural refinement, not a classification of all regular polygonal norms.
sources: AJMAA 20 (2023), No. 1, Art. 2, definitions and conclusion
